_about: Do not hand edit. Regenerate after regenerating the catalogue.
Catalogue seed 7, 15 listings, exhaustive 15 opens, oracle floor 11 opens.

tasks.note: Control. The answer is on the search page itself, so a card level probe should settle it in one or two actions. If this fails, the agent cannot read the search page at all and the gated results below mean nothing.
tasks.query: Go to {base}/catalogsearch/result/?q=Rivenhall . Of the Rivenhall water listings shown, which one advertises the lowest price on the results page, and what is that price?

tasks.note: The headline task. The lowest advertised price belongs to Hillside Wholesale, but the cheapest 2 x 9.5L is Redhill Stores. Answering from the search page alone gives the wrong seller.
tasks.query: Go to {base}/catalogsearch/result/?q=Rivenhall . Across all the Rivenhall listings, which seller is cheapest for the 2 x 9.5L pack, and what is that price?

tasks.note: Same retrieval, scored on the number rather than the seller name.
tasks.query: Go to {base}/catalogsearch/result/?q=Rivenhall . What is the lowest price anyone charges for the 2 x 9.5L pack of Rivenhall water?

tasks.note: 5 of 15 listings do not stock the target at all. Answering yes means the agent assumed every search result was comparable without checking.
tasks.query: Go to {base}/catalogsearch/result/?q=Rivenhall . Does every Rivenhall listing stock the 2 x 9.5L pack? Answer yes or no.

tasks.note: Needs every variant of every listing, so it is the most expensive question in the suite and the clearest test of whether the agent budgets its retrieval or simply gives up.
tasks.query: Go to {base}/catalogsearch/result/?q=Rivenhall . Across all the Rivenhall listings and all their pack sizes, which seller offers the lowest price per litre?
